findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-interop-psd/src/effects.rs:113-114 (closed tally checked before the counted total), :119-120 (a stack's own disabled instances can cross the uncounted total), :132-136 (an unrendered-cap refusal closes the tally for every later stack); src/proposal.rs:559-561; tests/effects_budget.rs:782-792 (asserts a VISIBLE Fx::live(1) stack Lost(effects_unrendered_over_document_budget) with a counted total of 0); src/lib.rs:82 DESCRIPTOR ('kept_instances_no_plan_counts_are_bounded_by_4096_loss_effects_unrendered_over_document_budget')
findings.evidence: Once the instances no plan counts (hidden layers/groups, master-off stacks, switched-off instances, including switched-off instances on VISIBLE layers) pass 4096 in panel order, the tally closes and every later non-empty stack is refused with effects_unrendered_over_document_budget, including visible stacks whose live instances a plan would render and whose counted budget is untouched; a visible stack with live instances is also refused when its own switched-off instances cross the uncounted total. So rendered effects are lost because of the count of unrendered instances, under a loss code that says 'unrendered', and the DESCRIPTOR string reads as if only the uncounted instances were bounded. This is the R9 concern (hidden/disabled instances decide the fate of rendered content) in a typed-loss form, not a whole-import failure. It is disclosed in the lane (capabilities_done 'same prefix cut', notes.remediation_R9.design 'prefix cut') before the lead decision 2026-10-11T14:41:47Z, which accepts the 4096 uncounted bound and panel-order cut but words the loss as 'hidden/disabled/master-off instances bounded with typed loss'. Frequency UNVERIFIED: whether Photoshop routinely stores switched-off effect instances in lfx2/lmfx (which would make the uncounted total grow with ordinary styled layers) was not checked against any Photoshop-authored file (D5).
findings.remediation: Either (a) lead confirms the 14:41:47Z decision covers rendered stacks lost under the unrendered cap and the DESCRIPTOR/ProposalConfig text says 'every later stack, rendered or not, is not mapped once either document total is passed'; or (b) close per category: an unrendered-cap crossing refuses later stacks only for their uncounted part (keep a visible stack's live instances and drop its switched-off ones with a Transformed loss, or refuse only stacks with uncounted > 0), with one test where 4097 hidden instances precede a visible live stack that stays Kept

A document whose switched-off/hidden instances exceed 4096 and which imported fully at f6e5a49 under a caller Budget::nodes >= records + instances now loses every stack from the crossing stack on (rendered ones included, see the CONFIRMED item). findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-reel/src/isobmff.rs:2011-2015 (slots keyed by media sample index: a sample presented twice keeps only its last presented entry), :2033-2067 (each sample index read and sunk once; delivered counts distinct samples), :2083 (actual.units = delivered), :2085-2089 (Exact for an exact start), :2099 (complete: true constant); build_presentation :1426-1481 pushes a sample once per edit whose media range covers it and build_edits :1351-1408 accepts overlapping media ranges (no check); @f6e5a49 isobmff.rs:1819-1822, :1907 (pre-existing)
findings.evidence: An edit list whose edits present the same media twice (e.g. a 4-sample track, 20 media units per sample, edits [(40, 0), (40, 0)] -> presented s0@0, s1@20, s0@40, s1@60 in media units) is indexed without refusal. Purpose::Export, OutputMode::Packets, an exact start 0 and count 4 passes require_exact_track_start (:1978); wanted holds four entries over two sample indexes, slots keep only the second edit's entries, the loop delivers 2 chunks (carrying the second edit's pts 40/60 while actual.start_pts is 0), and the call returns Ok with Disposition::Exact, complete: true and actual.units 2 of 4; report::outcome_for maps it to Success (report.rs:13). This contradicts DESCRIPTOR export.rule ('Purpose::Export is exact or it fails', lib.rs:87), the brief's behaviour contract ('fewer units delivered than requested -> typed error', lane-reel-eng-1.md topic api) and the lane's V4-06 class ('a delivery path that returns Ok with an Approximate, Partial or incomplete result without consulting req.purpose'), whose site list marks isobmff.rs:2099 'not applicable: constant, the delivery either completed or returned an error'. The decoded-video path over the same packets refuses correctly (Forward delivers fewer pictures -> Incomplete, video.rs:518-526), and isobmff PCM refuses multi-edit lists (pcm-edit-list-shape), so the gap is the packet path of isobmff (and of any Export remux built on it). Preview has the same silent shortfall reported as complete (pre-existing; STU-ARC-021). B3 adds one more reachable shape: a fragmented file whose open-ended last edit (isobmff.rs:1379) overlaps an earlier edit. Not hostile-only: overlapping edits are a well-formed edit list as far as this reader is concerned; how often real files carry them is UNVERIFIED.
findings.remediation: In deliver_packets emit one chunk per presented entry of `wanted` (re-read a repeated sample, or key slots by presented index) so delivered == count, or refuse a requested range that repeats a media sample (Export: typed error such as Unsupported edit-repeats-media / Incomplete; Preview: complete = false, Disposition::Partial); replace the constant complete: true by delivered == req.count; correct the V4-06 site verdict; one test: two-edit MOV repeating media, Packets Export and Preview, plus the decoded-video leg
